rationale: Asserts the field has long relied only on TPR/FPR; many works (e.g., WaterBench, WaterJudge, SynthID) also evaluate quality and robustness, so stated as settled overreach.
Meta framing of the subsection's own taxonomy; calls it 'empirically grounded' without evidence but carries no factual claim about others.
Asserts a non-linear watermark-strength/safety-guard trade-off as established; this comes from a single study (Watermarking Degrades Alignment) that is not cited here.
Declares a 'paradigm shift' to threat-coevolving benchmark ecosystems as fact; no cited benchmark is shown doing this.
Transition sentence restating previous and next subsections.

Claims contemporary benchmarks enforce survival through fine-tuning, distillation, quantization, speculative decoding and unlearning; no benchmark listed does all of this, and S0322 itself says no benchmark tracks fine-tuning trajectories.
States that friction 'manifests not in detection accuracy' as settled; a broad, unsupported generalisation.
Survey's framing that constraints are coupled; offered as analysis.
Asserts that technical validation assumes a monolithic English-dominant user as fact; plausible concern but stated as settled without evidence.
Framing of a shift toward certified evaluation; no specific factual content.
